summary: Swain County, NC fire tower in Great Smoky Mountains NP, built 1934 with PWA involvement; standing and reached on foot; last dated repair 2014, current condition unconfirmed.

facts.design: Steel tower about 60 feet tall with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab; 1934 ground cabin removed in 1987, chimney and cistern remain

staffing.status: manned by the National Park Service until decommissioned in the late 1960s

access.note: Reached on foot by the Appalachian Trail and a short spur trail; Wikipedia says the tower is accessible to the public; no closure notice found

visit.trail_note: About 3.4 to 3.5 miles on foot from the road or the north side of the Fontana Dam parking lot; rated medium to strenuous by the Smokies Guide; summit about 2,300 feet above Fontana Lake per Wikipedia

The county field held a state abbreviation; NHLR gives Swain County, North Carolina

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the PWA and the NPS constructed the tower in 1934; WillhiteWeb names only the PWA. Both agree on 1934 and PWA involvement, and the story follows them. A blog found in search credits the CCC, but it could not be opened (HTTP 403), so it is not relied on.

notes_for_editor: Brief corrections: state TN to NC and county NC to Swain. Builder conflict: thebraindump.blog credits the CCC; the page returned 403 and is not cited. Grokipedia and islands.com say PWA; not cited. Current condition is unverified: the newest dated work is the 2014 partial rehab. The Smoky Mountain News feature is undated in the cache and refers only to Barr's 2010 hike and the years after it, so the story gives it no date. The SMN article names Peter Barr, director of the N.C. chapter of the national Forest Fire Lookout Association; he is not identified with the NHLR nominator. 'Medium to strenuous' is from the Smokies Guide; Wikipedia gives only the roughly 2,300-foot rise, so the story no longer cites it for 'strenuous'. No source read states whether the stairs are currently safe or whether climbing is allowed, so the story advises checking with NPS. A Smokies Friends page from 2023 says the tower remains standing as one of four original park towers, but its URL is not in the cache, so it is not cited.
